method_notes: Offset -11 (pdf 12 = printed folio 1; pdf 77 = folio 66). Q side: q1-7 pdf12 (folio1, Section I), q8-23 pdf13 (folio2). A side: keys 1-19 pdf77 (folio66), keys 20-23 pdf78 (folio67). KEY ANSWERS section header pdf77; ch1 key monotonic 1-23, NO shift/insert/orphan/map (clean chapter).

Sections (question side, labels I-IV sequential, no defect): I Multiple Choice (q1-7, mcq) 'Identify the correct choice'; II one word or sentence (q8-16, vsa); III two or three sentences (q17-22, sa); IV five or six sentences (q23, la). Answer side keeps the same I-IV order and numbering; pairing by printed number is trivial.

DIFFICULTY tags are single letters (A)=average (E)=easy (D)=difficult (LETTERDIFF). DIFFICULTY-TABLE-VS-TAGS defect: printed table 18/2/3 (total 23); per-question tags 18/3/2 — Average and Difficult are swapped (table says A2/D3, tags say A3/D2), TOTAL agrees (23). quota_table difficulty_only, second_method total agrees, tags win (v2 §6 / addendum §8). Register difficulty-table-vs-tags.

MCQ q1-7 letter+text keys (addendum §4.1). q5 'B) Lavani' vs option B 'ballads (lavani)': letter B kept (answer asserted), benign flag 'key text differs from option by a printed typo' — NOT a typo, an abbreviation (Lavani = the ballad form); noted for review. q1 'Si-Yu-Ki'/'Si-yu-ki', q3 'Halmidi Inscription'/'Halmidi inscription', q7 'Buddha charita'/'Buddha Charita' are case-only, no flag.
VSA q8-16 answer.value = the sentence, no solution_steps (ruling 3d). q8 key printed with a trailing blank '___' (fill-in form) — kept verbatim.

Descriptive keys: q17-21,q23 SUB (a 'X:' heading line, NOT a step — addendum §5.2 / ruling 3b, kept in answer.value; the list items are the steps). q22 BUL (lead sentence 'The historians follow the various methods...' is a full topic sentence, not a colon-label heading → it is step 1, ruling 3b; then 5 bullets).

q17 four numbered points '1) .. 4)' printed two-per-line -> 4 steps (one per numbered point). q18/q19 bullets printed 2-3 per line in the text layer -> de-glued to one step per bullet (q18=4, q19=6). q20 six bullets one-per-line. q21 fifth bullet wraps across two printed lines -> merged into one step. De-glue applied in solution_steps/text only; q19 lead 'Literary Works of foreigners are' treated as a (colon-dropped) list heading, non-step — FLAG for coordinator ruling.

key-lines self-count (addendum §13.3): mcq 1-7 option keys; vsa 8-16 single-value (no steps); q17=4 steps+1 heading, q18=4+1, q19=6+1(lead-as-heading), q20=6+1, q21=5+1, q22=6 steps(lead+5 bullets, 0 heading), q23=6+1. Differences vs printed lines explained inline (numbered points 2/line q17; glued bullets q18/q19; wrapped bullet q21).

questions.text: Explain how literary sources contributes in construction of Indian history.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain how literary sources contributes in construction of Indian history. (A)

answer.value:
Literary Sources:
Written literature is classified into indigenous and foreign literature.
It reflects the history of the respective period.
It assists historians in analyzing historical information.
Indigenous literature includes works like Kautilya's Arthashastra, Hala's Gathasaptashati, Banabhatta's Harsha Charita, Pampa's Vikramarjuna Vijaya, Buddhist Tripitakas, and Shrivijaya's Kavirajamarga.
Foreign literature, such as Megasthenes' Indica and Hiuen Tsang's Si-Yu-Ki, provides substantial information.
Works like Ptolemy's Geography, Ceylon's Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa shows the light on dynasties, kings, their achievements and the socio-political conditions and wars of the time.
